chunks: 2546 - Ibn Bukayr narrated from Zurārah, who said:

I heard Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام say: “Whoever performs tawaf of the House and between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah becomes permitted [to exit iḥrām], if he wishes or dislikes it, except one who performed ʿumrah in that same year, or drove the sacrificial animal and marked it and garlanded it.”

key_terms.أَحَلَّ: became permitted, meaning exited the state of iḥrām
key_terms.قَلَّدَهُ: garlanded it as a marked sacrificial animal
key_terms.ٱلصَّفَا: al-Ṣafā, one of the two hills of saʿy
key_terms.ٱلْبَيْتِ: the Sacred House, meaning the Kaʿbah
key_terms.ٱلْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwah, the other hill of saʿy
key_terms.ٱلْهَدْيَ: the sacrificial animal offered in hajj rites

ai.seo_question: When does a pilgrim become permitted to exit iḥrām after tawaf and saʿy?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning release from the state of iḥrām after performing tawaf of the Kaʿbah and saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. It states a general rule of becoming permitted afterward, while excluding specific cases related to one who performed ʿumrah in that same year or one who brought and designated sacrificial animals.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2546 - Ibn Bukayr narrated from Zurara, who said:

I heard Abu Ja‘far (as) say:
"Whoever performs tawaf around the Ka‘bah and between Safa and Marwah becomes permitted (to exit the state of ihram) if they wish, whether willingly or unwillingly, except for the one who has performed ‘umrah in that same year or has driven the sacrificial animal (hady) and marked it (ash‘arah) and placed a garland (qalladah) on it."
